newsitem.title: UK: Iran candidate seen backing economic reforms.
newsitem.headline: Iran candidate seen backing economic reforms.

text.p: The front-running candidate for the Iranian presidency is expected to usher in a programme of economic reforms if he wins elections later this year, a senior Iranian politician said on Wednesday.

Mohammad Javad Larijani, deputy chairman of the Iranian Majlis (parliament) foreign relations committee, said he was backing the Majlis speaker Ali Akbar Nateq-Nouri in presidential polls due to be held in May or June.
Nateq-Nouri is seen as the leading candidate to succeed President Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani, who is barred from running after having served two four-year terms.
"I think if he wins the election he will be in a very good position to initiate important reform programmes," Larijani told a London news conference.
Larijani said Nateq-Nouri would invigorate the economy, implement a tight monetary policy, discipline the banks and increase security of investment.
Nateq-Nouri would also encourage private entrepreneurs, make the government withdraw from financial and economic activities and cut the size of the government.
"We do have a very fat, incompetent government," Larijani said. "Shrinking that will be a very painful process but a very important one."
Larijani said Nateq-Nouri differed from Rafsanjani because he wanted to press ahead more with the privatisation of state enterprises.
"Privatisation is an area that Nateq-Nouri is going to follow more forcefully than Mr Rafsanjani," Larijani said.
He said Rafsanjani was not opposed to privatisation, but had not made it a priority.
Nateq-Nouri was also more in favour of tight monetary policy than Rafsanjani.
"I think this will be also an important aspect of the economic package of Mr Nateq-Nouri," Larijani said.
Rafsanjani had preferred to initiate infrastructure projects rapidly, rather than keep a tight hold on monetary policy.

Larijani said a more disciplined approach to monetary policy would have a wide range of effects, especially on the Iranian banking system. If Nateq-Nouri was elected, the central bank would become more independent.

Asked about rumours that he might be foreign minister if Nateq-Nouri became president, Larijani, who is also a member of Iran's National Security Council, said he was happy with his present position in parliament.
"These are things that we will decide at the end," he said. "It is better not to speculate on that at this moment."
